records.title: The Multi-Agent Off-Switch Game
records.authors: Akash Agrawal; Soroush Ebadian; Lewis Hammond
records.venue: Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
records.key_contribution: Introduces the multi-agent off-switch game, generalizing Hadfield-Menell et al.'s single-agent framework. Shows that individually corrigible agents can become collectively incorrigible under strategic interaction (corrigibility does not compose across agents) and identifies conditions under which group incorrigibility emerges.
records.relevance_justification: Directly relevant: frames a safety property (corrigibility) as NON-compositional under multi-agent dynamics - a compositional-failure-meets-alignment-failure result closely analogous to the sigma-trap claim that compositional generalization failure and alignment failure share a mechanism.
records.open_questions: 1. Under what conditions does group incorrigibility emerge? 2. What mechanisms could restore collective corrigibility? 3. Extensions to partially observable or learning agents?
records.key_equations_definitions: Multi-agent off-switch game form (agent utility over switching); corrigibility composition result (corrigibility is not compositional).
records.notes: ft_file=The Multi-Agent Off-Switch Game.pdf; pilot=manual-review

records.title: Towards a societal AI alignment benchmark for evaluating human–machine value convergence

records.key_contribution: Reports a Likert-scale survey comparing sentiment of seven LLMs (including GPT-4) and humans toward AGI, using a societal AI alignment benchmark for evaluating human-machine value convergence. Provides empirical evidence on whether LLM values converge with societal attitudes toward AGI.
records.relevance_justification: Empirical evidence on value convergence between LLMs and humans - relevant background for whether surface-statistical value alignment tracks deeper value structure; does not address internal representation structure or compositional generalization.
records.open_questions: Whether LLM-human value convergence is robust across cultures and contexts; how survey-based alignment measurement relates to behavioral alignment.
records.datasets_used: Societal AI alignment benchmark; Likert-scale survey administered to 7 LLMs and human respondents
records.effect_sizes: Not reported in abstract (survey distributions reported in paper)
